notes: Page 2 has no building step. Panel 1 says to work on a table, not the floor. Panel 2 says to sort the pieces by colour (red, blue, yellow, grey/black) and to keep small parts and axles in their own pile. No pieces were placed.
Step 3 builds a minifigure (red cap, head, red postal torso, black legs). Its parts are not in the parts list, so I did not record them.

Hand truck step 1: the black wheel pair (lego-2496) goes onto the red frame's axle ends. Step 2: the parcel is a 2x2 dark grey brick with a 2x2 light grey tile on top. The tile carries a sticker, and the sticker is not recorded. The parcel is placed on the hand truck.
I assumed the black wheel pair is lego-2496. The tyres (3139) and wheel centres (3464) are not used on this page.
The parcel does not clutch any stud on the frame, so its only link to the frame is the loose join above.

Step 1: a dark grey wedge plate with a 2x2 cutout is placed at the end of the black 2x8 plate. I read the grey piece as lego-43719, because it is the only piece in the list that matches. It is a guess.

Step 2: the inset builds a dark grey 2x4 plate with a red 1x2 plate at two opposite corners. The inset then goes onto the black plate and wedge plate. I assumed the 2x4 plate clutches both, but the picture is unclear about exactly which studs it covers.
The 2x4 plate is a sub-assembly built first and then fitted. The ids are b7 for the 2x4 plate, b8 and b9 for the red 1x2 plates.

Step 3: a dark grey inverted 45° double slope with a 4x2 recess goes onto the black 2x8 plate from below. I read it as lego-4854, because the black plate sits in its recess in step 4. The studs of the slope clutch the underside of the black plate (b5). This is an interpretation, because the model is turned over in the pictures.

Step 4: the red 2x10 plate (lego-3832) lies across the fuselage as the wing. I listed only the new grey slope (b10) as its support. It may also touch the red 1x2 plates (b8, b9) and the wedge plate (b6), but the picture does not show this clearly.

Step 5: a yellow nose and two yellow side rows go on the side studs of the grey slope (b10) around the black plate. I read them as one yellow 3x4 wedge plate for the nose and two yellow 1x4 plates for the sides. This is a guess from the stud counts, because the pictures do not show the pieces clearly.

Step 6: two light grey 6x3 wedge plates are the wings, on top of the red 2x10 plate (b11). I took the far wing as the Right piece (54383) and the near wing as the Left piece (54384), with the nose pointing left in the picture. The wings could also touch other pieces, but I recorded only b11.

Step 7: a red wedge plate 3x4 covers the yellow nose wedge. Two red 1x8 plates run along the two sides over the yellow 1x4 plates and the wing roots. The 1x8 length is a guess from the number of studs, because the strips look longer than the yellow 1x4 plates. Which yellow plate is on which side is also a guess. The 1x8 plates also overlap the grey wing plates, so I listed those too (b15 on the far side, b16 on the near side).

Step 8: the model is turned upside down, so the wing undersides and the underside of the plane body are visible. The dark grey pieces seen are ones already placed (b6, b7, b10). I think this step adds only one red 1x2 plate, which goes on the dark grey 2x4 plate (b7). The picture is hard to read, so this is an assumption.

Step 9: two red 1x4 plates lie across the back of the opening, one beside the other, on the two red 1x8 plates (b18, b19). The blue tile with handle (the control stick) goes into the cockpit opening on the black plate (b5). I assumed it clutches b5 only.

Step 10: a grey 2x2 plate with a wheel holder is added at the front edge of each wing. I read both as lego-4488, which is a guess because the picture is small. The small pin sticking out of each is probably where a propeller will go, so I did not record it as a join. A trans-green round plate goes at the far wing tip (b15) and a trans-red one at the near wing tip (b16). Green on the right wing and red on the left wing matches real aircraft lighting.

Step 11: each engine gets two yellow curved 3x1 bricks, one on the wheel-holder plate and one behind it on the wing studs. The arrows show the second brick on the far side going onto two wing studs. The near side is shown finished, so I copied the far-side layout for it (4 curved bricks in the parts list).
The curved bricks may overlap both the engine plate and the wing studs, but I listed only the main support for each.

Step 12: a yellow tapered wedge brick (lego-4858) forms the nose. It has two studs on the tip, which matches the two studs seen. A yellow 1x3 brick goes on each side of the cockpit as a wall. Which wall is on which red 1x8 plate (b18, b19) is a guess. The two yellow 1x2x1 panels (4865a) may also be part of the walls here, but I could not see them clearly, so I left them for a later page.

Step 13: a white 2x2 brick goes on the cockpit floor, with the white sloped 2x2 instrument panel (flight controls print) on top. I read the brick as lego-3003 in White. The remaining-parts list no longer shows the white one, so the lists are inconsistent. The dark grey 3003 from page 3 is still listed, and the white brick in this picture is not. I assumed the white brick clutches the black plate (b5) only.

Step 14 (2x): each yellow 1x4 window gets two glass panes pushed into its openings. The windows are built first and then placed on the sides of the cockpit, one per side. The far window sits on the far red 1x8 plate (b18) and the near window on the near one (b19). The side wall bricks from step 12 sit next to them, but I did not list them as support here.
Each 60601 glass is joined to its window by a slide-in join, listed in other_joins. It has no stud ports, so it rests on nothing.
The plane is now shown with the nose at the left and the tail at the right.

Step 15: a long dark grey inverted slope forms the tail. I chose lego-4856a (6x4) from its size and tapering shape. It goes on the small dark grey wedge plate (b6) at the back of the fuselage. This is a guess, because lego-4855 is another possible match.

Step 16: a red U-shape covers the tail slope. I read it as a red 3x4 wedge plate for the tip and two red 1x4 plates for the arms, the same layout as the nose on page 7. The stud counts are the only evidence for this. I listed the grey tail piece (b43) as the only support. The red parts may also touch the red cross plates (b21, b22) next to them.

Step 17 has no arrows, so I worked out the new pieces by comparing it with step 16. Two yellow rows with studs appear on the red 1x8 plates behind the windows. I read them as the two yellow 1x2x1 panels (4865a), one per side. This is a guess, because I count three studs in each row and a panel has only two.
A raised red block appears at the tail, on top of the red tail plates. I read it as the red 3x4 wedge brick lego-50373. It sits on the red wedge plate and the two red 1x4 plates (b44, b45, b46).

Step 18: the trans-blue windscreen goes over the cockpit, on the yellow nose (b32) and the two yellow side walls (b33, b34). This is read from the picture, because the windscreen covers the cockpit front.

Step 19: a dark grey 1x6 tile goes on the near side, over the near window (b38) and the yellow panel behind it (b48). A dark grey hinge tile 1x4 (with its two fingers on top) goes on the far window (b37). The hinge tile fingers are probably for a hatch on a later page, so I recorded no hinge join yet. The tile lengths fit the windows plus the panel, but this is a guess.

Step 20 has no arrows. Comparing it with the last picture, the only new piece is a white 2x2 plate on the top of the tail, in front of the red tail block (b49). I assumed it sits on the two red 1x4 tail plates (b45, b46). I could not tell exactly which pieces it clutches.
Step 21 has no arrows and no new piece. It shows the model from the nose side to check the build so far. The pieces I can see are all ones placed on earlier pages, so I added nothing.

Step 22 has no arrows. Comparing it with step 21, a dark grey sloped piece with four studs is new on the top of the tail. I read it as lego-4855, one of the two dark grey 4x4 inverted slopes still in the list. I assumed it sits on the red tail block (b49) and the red wedge plate (b44).

A light grey wedge plate 4x9 (lego-2413) sticks up and back from the tail as the fin. I assumed it clutches the studs of the new dark grey tail piece. The picture is unclear about this, and the second 2413 is probably the matching tail piece in a later step.

Step 23 has no parts box, so I read the new pieces from the picture and the shrinking parts list. The second light grey 4x9 wedge plate (b56) is the other half of the tail plane. The first half (b55) was added on page 17. I assumed it also clutches the dark grey tail piece (b54).

The yellow wedged slope (lego-48933) covers the tail top and the yellow tail fin (lego-6239) stands up at the back. Both are assumed to sit on b54. The tail fin has no stud ports in the catalogue, so I could not tell how it clutches.
The yellow 3x4 double slope (lego-4861) is the near roof piece over the cockpit. I assumed it sits on the near wall brick (b34).

The yellow 4x4 slope with a locking hinge (lego-44571) is the roof hatch. It is joined to the dark grey hinge tile (b52) with a hinge. The arrow shows it swinging down. Once it is closed, it may also clutch b52 and the studs below it, but I recorded only the hinge.

Step 24 (3x): each wheel is a black tyre pushed onto a white wheel centre, and the wheel centre is clipped into a light grey 2x2 wheel holder. The model is upside down in the picture, so the three holders go on the underside of the plane.

I put one holder at the nose on the grey slope (b10) and two near the wing roots, on the red 1x2 plates (b8, b9) and the grey 2x4 plate (b7). The picture does not show exactly which studs they clutch, so this is a guess.
The tyres and wheel centres have no studs, so they rest on nothing and are linked only by the joins above.

Step 25 is the finished plane with the pilot minifigure going into the cockpit and the canopy (windscreen with roof) being put on. The minifigure is not in the parts list, so I did not record it. The canopy pieces were already placed (b50, b59), so nothing new is added for them.
The two black propellers (lego-2421) are on the pins at the front of the two engine plates (b24, b25). I did not record the pins as parts.
The grey antenna (lego-298c02, lever small base) sits on the studs of the yellow roof slope (b59). This is an assumption, because the picture is small.

Stickers appear on the tail fin and fuselage, but I did not record them as pieces. The leftover parts (red plates, red wedge plate, grey inverted slope, cheese slopes, grey tile, red inverted slope) are not used by this model, so they are probably for a second model on the next pages.
Page 21 is the parts list with element numbers and counts. No building step, so nothing was placed.

The nine part lines still unplaced are the leftover parts of the plane build, and I did not place them on any earlier page. They are a red 2x2 plate, a red 1x2 plate, a dark grey 1x2 tile, a red 1x4 plate, a red inverted slope, a red 3x4 wedge plate, a dark grey inverted slope, four yellow cheese slopes and the sticker sheet. They may be used on the next pages, or I may have misread an earlier step.
Page 22 is an advert for the LEGO City sets 7731, 7732, 7733 and 7734. There is no building step, so nothing was placed.
Page 23 is an advert for the LEGO Club and the LEGO shop. There is no building step, so nothing was placed.
Page 24 is a competition advert with other LEGO sets and the copyright line. There is no building step, so nothing was placed.

Nine part lines in the list were never placed in this recording. Pages 3 to 20 account for the rest of the plane build. These are the parts not placed: 1 red 2x2 plate, 1 red 1x2 plate, 1 dark grey 1x2 groove tile, 1 red 1x4 plate, 1 red inverted slope 3x2, 1 red 3x4 wedge plate, 1 dark grey inverted wedge slope 4x4, 4 yellow cheese slopes and the sticker sheet. The booklet pictures do not show them in the plane. They may be spares, or I may have read some of the earlier steps wrongly.

Two groups: the booklet really builds two separate models. Page 3 builds a hand truck with a parcel (b1 to b4), and pages 4 to 20 build the mail plane. The two are never joined (the final picture shows the hand truck standing next to the plane). I kept them as two groups on purpose.

Nine part lines were still unplaced: red 2x2 plate, red 1x2 plate, dark grey 1x2 groove tile, red 1x4 plate, red inverted slope 3x2, red 3x4 wedge plate, dark grey inverted wedge slope 4x4, four yellow cheese slopes and the sticker sheet. I added them to match the parts list, but I could not find where the booklet pictures put them, so every placement below is a guess.

Placement guesses: red 2x2 and red 1x2 plates on the grey 2x4 plate (b7) under the wing roots. Red 1x4 plate on the red wing plate (b11). Red wedge plate on the grey slope (b10). Red inverted slope (3747b) under the tail slope (b43). Dark grey 4855 on the black fuselage plate (b5). Dark grey tile on the white tail plate (b53). Two cheese slopes on the yellow nose (b32) and two on the yellow tail slope (b57). These pieces may belong in places I misread, such as the red parts near the wing roots in step 8. The sticker sheet is recorded as one part stuck on the tail fin (b58).
The checker also said 'not in the list'. I found no piece of mine with a type missing from the parts list, so I did nothing about that.

The two separate groups are real, so I added no connection. Set 7732 builds two models. Page 3 builds a hand truck with a parcel (b1 to b4). Pages 4 to 20 build the mail plane (everything else). In the final picture on page 20 the hand truck stands on the ground beside the plane and does not touch it. No step joins them, so any edge between them would be invented.

The hand truck group is connected inside itself: the parcel brick and tile are joined to the frame, and the wheels are on the frame axle. The plane group is also fully connected, including the wheels, propellers, hatch and sticker.
